skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Guide branch completion after tests pass by choosing local merge, pull request, keep, or discard workflows with cleanup safeguards.
skill.summary: Guides final Git integration choices after implementation and tests are complete.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported 24 issues, but each was a false positive: Markdown fences, safe shell substitutions, or stderr redirection in examples. I found no prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or semantic abuse; destructive Git cleanup is explicitly gated by user confirmation.

content.value_statement: Completed branches need a clear path to merge, pull request, retention, or cleanup. This skill guides test verification, choice presentation, and guarded Git completion workflows.
actual_capabilities: Verifies that tests pass before offering integration choices.
Finds a likely base branch with git merge-base or asks the user to confirm.
Presents four clear options: local merge, pull request, keep branch, or discard work.
Creates a pull request workflow with a summary and test plan template.
Requires typed confirmation before deleting a branch or worktree.
Cleans worktrees after merge or confirmed discard workflows.
limitations: Requires a local Git repository with the relevant branches available.
Needs the project test command or enough context to choose one.
Pull request creation depends on GitHub CLI access and authentication.
Does not resolve merge conflicts or failing tests without additional work.

use_cases.title: Complete a feature branch
use_cases.description: Verify tests, choose the correct finish path, and avoid ambiguous end-of-work decisions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a team pull request
use_cases.description: Push the current branch and create a pull request with a concise summary and test plan.

use_cases.title: Clean a temporary worktree
use_cases.description: Remove a completed or discarded worktree only after the selected workflow makes cleanup appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Finish my branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after implementation is complete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use finishing-a-development-branch to verify tests and present completion options for my current branch.

prompt_templates.title: Create a pull request
prompt_templates.scenario: Contributor wants review instead of a local merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use finishing-a-development-branch. After tests pass, push this branch and draft a pull request with summary and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Merge and clean locally
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants the branch integrated into the base branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use finishing-a-development-branch to confirm the base branch, merge locally, rerun tests, and clean up the finished branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review risky cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user needs careful handling before deletion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use finishing-a-development-branch to inspect the branch, list commits before discard, and wait for exact confirmation before destructive actions.

output_examples.input: I finished the feature and tests pass.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the test result, identifies the base branch, and offers merge, pull request, keep, or discard options.
The assistant pushes the branch, drafts a pull request summary and test plan, then preserves the worktree.
The assistant lists what will be deleted and waits for the exact discard confirmation before deletion.

best_practices: Run the full project test suite before choosing a completion path.
Confirm the base branch when the detected branch is unexpected.
Review branch commits and worktree paths before typing discard confirmation.
anti_patterns: Using the skill before implementation and tests are complete.
Selecting discard as quick cleanup without reviewing deleted work.
Assuming GitHub CLI pull request creation works without authentication.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides the final step after development: verify tests, choose a finish path, and handle Git cleanup.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to run the project test suite before offering merge or pull request options.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a workflow for pushing the branch and creating a pull request with GitHub CLI.

faq.question: Will it delete branches?
faq.answer: Only if the user selects discard and types the exact confirmation requested by the workflow.

faq.question: Does it support Git worktrees?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for worktree usage and removes worktrees only for merge or confirmed discard paths.

faq.question: Is it suitable for team repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but team branch protection, review rules, and release policies still apply.
